Double brackets mark a word with a definition from the glossary ([[word]] or [[glossary key|shown text]]). A quoted item is {"from": "file.field", "pick": "text inside one sentence"} and shows that sentence of the data as it stands; "cut" ends it at that character. title: Today's wars
intro: A first look at the wars being fought now, one idea at a time. The map is built up as you scroll.
asof: Wars and lines as of {as_of}. Deaths counted by UCDP to {ucdp_reach}.

glossary.UCDP: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program, a university project in Sweden that counts armed conflicts and the deaths in them, year by year.
glossary.armed conflict: A fight between a government and an opposing side in which at least {acd_bar} people died that year.
glossary.band: A range a death count falls in. {band_ranges}
glossary.armed group: A fighting force that is not the army of a state: a rebel movement, a militia, a gang, a jihadist group.
glossary.backer: A state, a group of states, or a force that runs part of a state, that helps one side from outside the war.
glossary.attribution: Saying who did something, and on what evidence.
glossary.province: The first level of division inside a country. Some countries call them states or regions.
glossary.provisional: Not final. UCDP revises its latest years as more reports come in.

steps.name: how many
steps.title: How many wars are there right now?
steps.body: This page builds a map of the wars of the past year, one layer at a time. Start with a guess.
steps.reveal: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), a university project in Sweden, counted {ucdp_n} [[armed conflict|armed conflicts]] in {ucdp_year}. Its bar is {acd_bar} deaths in a year. {ucdp_wars} of them reached {war_bar} deaths, the level it calls war. This map holds {wars} wars from the past twelve months. Its rule: {rule} The number depends on the rule.

sources.text: UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset, version {acd_version}, {n_first} to {ucdp_year}.
Every year since {n_first}, on one axis, is on the level page.

steps.name: where
steps.title: Where they are
steps.body: Each dot is one war. They arrive one region at a time: {region_counts}. Hover or tap a dot for its name.

sources.text: Each war, its point and its region are kept by hand in data/conflicts.json, as of {as_of}.

steps.name: a war is not a country
steps.title: A war is not a country
steps.body: Sudan's war began in {sudan_start}. The shaded provinces are where the fighting was in the past year, {sudan_prov} of them. A [[province]] is shaded for ground fighting, sieges or an air campaign. {areas_drone}
steps.toggle_text: Across the map, {areas_total} provinces are shaded in {areas_wars} wars. {areas_border}

steps.name: how big
steps.title: How big
steps.body: So far every dot is the same size. Before they take their size, a second guess.

guess.question: Which of these three killed the most people in the past year?

steps.reveal: The dots now take their size, for deaths in the past year, in three [[band|bands]]. [[UCDP]] counted {opt_counts} from {win_from} to {win_to}. Counts differ. For {wide_n} of the {wars} wars UCDP's own high is more than twice its low.
steps.chart_caption: Deaths by war, {win_from} to {win_to}, UCDP's best count. The thin line runs from its low to its high.

sources.pick: Deaths are shown as a band

sources.text: Each war's count adds up UCDP's records for the countries it covers, or for its named conflicts. Recent months are UCDP's candidate records, which it has not fully reviewed.

steps.name: who fights
steps.title: Who fights
steps.body: In Sudan two sides fight: the {sudan_a} and the {sudan_b}. The first is the army of a [[state]]. The second is an [[armed group]]. Most conflicts have that shape. Of the {ucdp_n} UCDP counted in {ucdp_year}, {interstate} were between states. In the other {intra}, a government fought an armed group.

units.rest: {intra} a government against an armed group
units.caption: UCDP's {ucdp_n} armed conflicts in {ucdp_year}, one square each

steps.name: who helps
steps.title: Who helps from outside
steps.body: Each line is a [[backer]] helping one side from outside the war. {sudan_backers} backers help a side in Sudan now. The list names the help each one gives. Some of this help is announced by the backer. Some is denied.
steps.toggle_text: A war is on this map only if an outside state fights in it or backs a side. Across the {wars} wars on the map, {lines_n} lines run from {backers_n} backers.

sources.text: Every line, with its sources, is in the table on the full map.

steps.name: how do we know
steps.title: How anyone knows
steps.body: Some help is announced. Some is denied and found anyway. Each line is graded on a ladder of [[attribution]], and the grade is drawn in the line: {tier_words}. The more broken the line, the weaker the public evidence for it.

guess.label: of every ten lines
guess.question: Out of every ten lines, how many are on the record?

steps.reveal: {open_n} of the {lines_n} lines are on the record, about {open_tenths} in ten. {most_open} {shown_n} are documented, {reported_n} reported and {claimed_n} alleged. {ended_n} more have ended and are drawn faint and dotted.
steps.most_open: Most help is given in the open.
steps.chips_cue: Tap a grade to hide its lines. Tap an example to find it on the map.

shown.pick: The evidence is in a public document

claimed.pick: Only a side in the fight says so

sources.pick: A finding by a state that fights

sources.text: The full rules for each grade are on the full map.

steps.name: the same states
steps.title: The same states, war after war
steps.body: Some states turn up in war after war. From here the {hued_n} states in the most wars each get a color. Pick one to light its lines.
steps.pick_line: {state_name} is in {state_in} of the {wars} wars. It fights in {state_fights} and backs a side in {state_backs}.
steps.pick_line_backs: {state_name} is in {state_in} of the {wars} wars. It backs a side in each and fights in none.
steps.both_live: In {war_name} it has lines to both sides.
steps.both_ended: In {war_name} it backs {live_party}. It backed {ended_party} until {ended_month}.

pair.lead: States on the same side in one war can be on opposite sides in the next.

vetted.pick: Egypt and Türkiye are on one side

sources.text: The grid of every state against every war is on the full map.

steps.name: force short of war
steps.title: Force short of war
steps.body: Some force stops short of war: strikes, raids, seizures, a blockade. None has sustained fighting, so none is on the map as a war. Each hollow square is one. There are {squares}, {sq_us} of them by the {us_name}. A square is on the map only if the state doing it has said so. The squares have their own lines of help, listed on the full map.

sources.pick: A state is also on the map

steps.name: is this normal
steps.title: Is this level normal?
steps.body: The map shows {wars} wars from one year. To look back, this chart uses UCDP's wider count of armed conflicts, which goes back to {n_first}. In {ucdp_year} it counted {ucdp_n}, {n_phrase}. On UCDP's best count the five years to {avg_last_year} average {avg_latest} deaths a year. {avg_two} The last {prov_word} years are [[provisional]].

phrases.n_tie: as many as the highest year before it
phrases.n_else: more than in all but {n_above} years
phrases.avg_two: The five years to {avg_other_year} average {avg_other}. Those are the two highest in the series. In {peak_year}, {peak_top_n} of that year's {peak_total} deaths were in {peak_top_name}.
phrases.avg_else: The highest five years in the series end in {avg_max_year}, at {avg_max} a year.

chart.bottom: Deaths a year in organized violence, {d_first} to {d_last}. Bars: UCDP's best count. Line: five-year average.

sources.pick: UCDP's best, low and high estimates

sources.text: Every year on one axis, with the oil price and what each peak was, is on the level page.

steps.name: the {wars_word} wars
steps.title: The {wars_word} wars
steps.body: One card for each war. The dot is its size. Next to it, how many sides fight and how many backers help. The strip is its lines, from on the record to alleged. Tap a card and the map goes there.

sources.text: Each war's full card, with every line and source, is on the full map.

steps.name: now it is yours
steps.title: Now it is yours
steps.body: The map is free. Drag it, zoom it, tap any war. The switches below turn layers on and off.
steps.hint_desktop: drag to move · ctrl + scroll or pinch to zoom · tap a war
steps.hint_phone: two fingers to move and zoom · tap a war
